title: Faucet drips from the spout when turned off (cartridge or washer)
text:
Tenant-safe troubleshooting (do in order):
1) Turn the handle fully off; on two-handle faucets, check both handles.
2) Put a cup under the spout to see how fast it drips.
3) Unscrew the aerator at the tip of the spout by hand, rinse out any grit, and screw it back on hand-tight.
4) If it still drips, close the shut-off valves under the sink (clockwise) when you're not using the tap.
5) Do not take the handle or cartridge apart: a plumber will replace the cartridge or washer.
Stop and escalate immediately if:
- Water runs steadily and won't stop with the handle off
- The handle is stuck or spins freely
- Water is reaching the cabinet or an outlet
What to send us (photos/video):
- Short video of the drip with the tap off
- Photo of the faucet and handle
- Photo of the shut-off valves under the sink

title: Leak at the drain pipe / P-trap under the sink
text:
Tenant-safe troubleshooting (do in order):
1) Don't run the tap or the dishwasher; put a bowl under the curved drain pipe (P-trap).
2) Dry the pipes with a towel, then run a little water and watch where the drop forms.
3) If it comes from a plastic slip nut (the large ring joints), tighten it by hand only, a quarter turn. No tools.
4) Run a little water again; if it still leaks, stop using the sink and leave the bowl in place.
Stop and escalate immediately if:
- The pipe is cracked or a joint has come apart
- Water backs up into the sink or dishwasher
- The cabinet floor is soaked or soft
What to send us (photos/video):
- Photo under the sink showing the P-trap
- Short video of where the water appears while draining

title: Leak at a supply hose or shut-off valve under the sink
text:
Tenant-safe troubleshooting (do in order):
1) Close both shut-off valves under the sink: turn clockwise until snug. Don't force them.
2) Put a bowl under the drip and towels on the cabinet floor.
3) Check whether the drip stops once the valves are closed.
4) Leave the valves closed and don't use the sink until it's repaired.
Stop and escalate immediately if:
- The valve won't close or the leak continues with the valves closed
- A hose is bulging, split or spraying
- Water is spreading beyond the cabinet
What to send us (photos/video):
- Photo of both valves and hoses
- Video showing whether the leak stops after closing the valves

title: Garbage disposal jammed or humming
text:
Tenant-safe troubleshooting (do in order):
1) Turn the disposal switch off. Never put your hand inside the disposal.
2) Wait 10 minutes for the motor to cool.
3) Press the red reset button on the bottom of the unit.
4) Run cold water and turn the switch on for a few seconds.
5) If it still only hums, turn it off and leave it off.
Stop and escalate immediately if:
- It smells like burning or the switch trips the breaker
- Water is leaking from the unit
- Something is stuck that you can't see from above
What to send us (photos/video):
- Short video of the sound when switched on
- Photo of the unit under the sink

title: Garbage disposal leaking
text:
Tenant-safe troubleshooting (do in order):
1) Don't run the disposal or the tap. Never put your hand inside it.
2) Put a bowl under the unit and towels on the cabinet floor.
3) Note where the drip forms: top (sink flange), side (dishwasher hose or drain pipe) or bottom (the unit itself).
4) Leave the sink unused until it's checked.
Stop and escalate immediately if:
- Water keeps coming even with the tap off
- Water is near the plug or the outlet under the sink
What to send us (photos/video):
- Photo of the unit from below
- Photo showing where the water drips

title: Dishwasher drain hose leaking under the sink
text:
Tenant-safe troubleshooting (do in order):
1) Don't run the dishwasher until it's checked.
2) Put a bowl under the hose connection under the sink (at the disposal or the drain pipe).
3) Check that the hose clamp looks seated; do not remove it.
4) If water appears only at the end of a cycle, note that: it's the drain hose.
Stop and escalate immediately if:
- The hose is cracked or has come off
- Water is spreading or near the outlet under the sink
What to send us (photos/video):
- Photo of the hose connection under the sink
- Video during a drain if safe

title: Toilet tank keeps filling or hissing (fill valve)
text:
Tenant-safe troubleshooting (do in order):
1) Lift the tank lid and look: is water flowing into the overflow tube?
2) If so, gently lift the float arm or float cup; if the water stops, the fill valve needs adjusting or replacing.
3) If the flapper at the bottom isn't sealing, jiggle the handle once.
4) If it keeps running, turn off the toilet's valve behind it (clockwise) between uses.
Stop and escalate immediately if:
- Water overflows the tank or the bowl
- The shut-off valve won't turn
What to send us (photos/video):
- Photo inside the tank (lid off)
- Short video of the running water

title: Range hood fan, light or filter problems
text:
Tenant-safe troubleshooting (do in order):
1) Check the fan and light switches on the hood and try each speed.
2) Check the breaker for the kitchen; reset it once if it has tripped.
3) If the light is out, let it cool and check whether the bulb is loose or burned out.
4) If grease drips or the fan is weak, let it cool, slide out the metal grease filter and wash it in hot soapy water; dry and put it back.
5) Don't take the hood apart or reach into the fan.
Stop and escalate immediately if:
- Burning smell, smoke, sparks or a buzzing switch
- The breaker trips again
- Oil dripping onto the stove that won't stop
What to send us (photos/video):
- Photo of the hood and its switches
- Short video of the fan sound
- Photo of the model label (inside, behind the filter)

title: Water heater relief (T&P) valve dripping
text:
Tenant-safe troubleshooting (do in order):
1) Keep clear of the pipe from the side of the tank: the water can be very hot.
2) Put a bucket under the end of the pipe.
3) Do not open, close or cap the relief valve.
4) Don't touch the gas controls or the burner area.
Stop and escalate immediately if:
- Steady flow or steam from the relief pipe
- Rumbling or banging from the tank
- Any smell of gas
What to send us (photos/video):
- Photo of the tank's side pipe
- Photo of the label on the tank

title: Water escaping the tub or shower (caulking, door or curtain)
text:
Tenant-safe troubleshooting (do in order):
1) Keep the curtain inside the tub, or the door fully closed, while showering.
2) Dry the floor after each shower and note where water collects.
3) Look for gaps or black lines in the caulking around the tub and corners.
4) If water shows on the ceiling below, stop using the shower until it's checked.
Stop and escalate immediately if:
- Water stains or drips on the ceiling below
- The floor is soft or tiles are loose
What to send us (photos/video):
- Photo of the caulking around the tub
- Photo of where water collects on the floor

title: Tub spout or shower head drips when off
text:
Tenant-safe troubleshooting (do in order):
1) Turn the handle firmly to fully off.
2) If there's a diverter (pull-up knob on the spout), push it down after showering.
3) Note whether it drips from the spout, the shower head, or both.
4) Don't take the handle or valve apart.
Stop and escalate immediately if:
- Water runs steadily and won't stop
- The handle won't turn off or spins freely
What to send us (photos/video):
- Short video of the drip
- Photo of the handle and spout
